About Me

Hey!

You've made it this far, so you must know enough about my journey. Thank you for taking your time browsing my portfolio. I must say that this portal is just the beginning of many more propulsion systems and exciting aerospace hardware projects to add onto.

I'm a propulsion-focused aerospace engineer who loves injector hydrodynamics, thermo-fluid simulation, and hardware design from first principles. From optimizing a 1000 N hypergolic satellite pintle injector at ISRO (LPSC) and diagnosing high-altitude LCA Tejas fuel/oil filtration thermal lock at DRDO (CVRDE), to designing 7 bar swirl coaxial & gas generator impinging injectors at ThrustWorks Dynetics, my drive toward rocket engines and spacecraft systems has grown exponentially.

Graduating with a First Class B.Tech in Aerospace Engineering (CGPA 8.11/10) from Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science has brought me closer toward my goal of engineering flight-ready propulsion hardware, backed by custom Python 14-geometry sizing tools, OpenFOAM/CFDForge™/ANSYS simulations, and cold-flow testing.

Apart from core propulsion engineering, I founded CMB (cmb-space.com)—a comprehensive Space Portal featuring aerospace blogs, motivation, and technical resources—and manage an active aerospace & defence community on Telegram (@VY0MANAUT).

Project A: Swirl Coaxial & Gas Generator Impinging Injectors

Developed a custom Python sizing application from scratch to evaluate, rank, and cross-check 14 distinct candidate injector geometries prior to manufacturing and cold-flow spray cone validation.

Project B: 1000 N Hypergolic Satellite Pintle Injector

Optimized a 1000 N thrust pintle injector for bipropellant satellite propulsion (MMH / N₂O₄). Modeled in SolidWorks, fabricated via precision CNC machining & TIG welding, and validated multiphase atomization in ANSYS CFX (+15% flow uniformity).

Project C: KNDX & KNSU Solid Rocket Motors & C-D Nozzles

Designed and simulated Dextrose (KNDX) and Sucrose (KNSU) composite solid rocket motors in OpenMotor to loft a 3.5 kg payload to a 200 m apogee. Modeled inhibits, BATES grain regression, and supersonic converging-diverging (C-D) nozzle contours.
